rules.recovers: functions referenced only by pointers whose neighbour below is already known
rules.restsOn: the linker lays compiled functions out back to back, each aligned with zero or nop padding
rules.summary: a valid candidate that starts where claimed bytes end, give or take padding, is a function

rules.recovers: nearby calls misread as far jumps, which would glue a neighbouring function into the caller
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits bl as a jump only when the target is beyond the range of `b`; the shortest far jump in five ROMs is 1,960 bytes
rules.summary: a bl closer than farJump.minDistance to its target (the far-jump idiom fails) is a call

rules.recovers: functions proposed inside another function's unreached branch arms or alignment padding
rules.restsOn: a compiled function is one contiguous run, so the few bytes inside it the walk never reached are still its own
rules.summary: a dense function's free bytes inside its extent are claimed as dead code

rules.recovers: the call graph below every accepted function
rules.restsOn: a bl (or a bx after mov lr, pc) that settles as a call enters a function
rules.summary: the targets of the calls of an accepted function are functions

rules.recovers: functions reached only through a pointer that accepted code loads
rules.restsOn: compiled code takes the address of a Thumb function as a pool word holding func+1 (callbacks, tables of handlers)
rules.summary: Thumb pointers loaded from the pools of accepted functions are candidate functions

rules.recovers: two functions glued into one by a tail branch, and claims of another function's code
rules.restsOn: a function never jumps into another function except as a tail call; agbcc and hand-written code share epilogues only by tail branches
rules.summary: a branch into another function or claimed code (ARM: or below the entry) is a tail exit
